label: rs-encode-ntt-simt-cuda
note: BabyBear RS [16384,4096] encoder as batched radix-2 NTT in shared memory (cupy RawKernel, Montgomery, 1 INTT + 3 coset NTTs per row, systematic): Candidate B shape 310,602 rows = 20.36 GB codeword in 39.3 ms/batch = 0.13 us/row = 9.6 us/VU; 518 GB/s of codeword, 648 GB/s HBM = 0.64 of the read+write roofline (25.2 ms); 778 G butterflies/s. A shape 6.1 ms. Bit-exact vs numpy reference. Beats the fused INT8 tensor-core matrix DFT 4.4x and the cost model rs_matrix_ntt@0.172 (413 ms) 10x: B encoding is memory-bound SIMT work, not tensor-core work.

label: rs-encode-matdft-int8-triton-fused
note: Two-stage 64x64 matrix DFT with fused INT8 limbs on tensor cores (Triton, one program per row, 16 tl.dot per stage, INT64 recombination in registers; 4 DFTs per row coset form, 33.6M limb MACs/row): B shape 171.5 ms/batch = 0.55 us/row = 41.9 us/VU, 60.8 T MAC/s = 0.184 of INT8 peak (tensor-core floor at 100%: 31.6 ms, itself 1.25x the HBM floor). Bit-exact. 4.4x slower than the SIMT NTT.

label: rs-encode-matdft-int8-cublas-unfused
note: Same matrix DFT via torch._int_mm (cuBLASLt) with the DFT-matrix limb tensor resident and only rows decomposed per call: 49 us/row (measured on 8192 rows, scaled) = 15.2 s per B batch, 0.002 of INT8 peak: the INT32 intermediates (64 B per element per stage), limb splits, transposes and recombination are each an HBM pass (1.4 TB per batch). Bit-exact. Unusable.
